claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa.
The baseline alloy has limited plasticity due in part to its high Mo content.
Approximately 50% of the Mo content should be replaced with Ta.
The proposed modified composition is NbZrTiHf(Mo0.5Ta0.5), corresponding to Nb20Zr20Ti20Hf20Mo10Ta10 in atomic percent.
Arc melting and homogenization can preserve a disordered BCC structure in the modified alloy.
Partial replacement of Mo with Ta will reduce the alloy's overall electronegativity difference.
The Mo-to-Ta substitution will maintain a similar atomic-size disparity.
Ta has a lower electronegativity than Mo.
Reducing electronegativity contrast will reduce localized bonding heterogeneities that impede dislocation motion.
Reduced dislocation pinning will enhance room-temperature plasticity.
Retained atomic-size mismatch and random lattice distortion will continue to provide high strength.
The modified alloy will have greater compressive strain to failure than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will retain a room-temperature compressive yield strength approximately equal to 1719 MPa.
The predicted strength-plasticity balance depends on retaining the disordered BCC structure and avoiding secondary phases.
Secondary-phase formation may invalidate the predicted strength-plasticity balance.

contradictions.description: The modified composition is called an equiatomic five-element alloy, but NbZrTiHf(Mo0.5Ta0.5) contains six chemical elements and is not equiatomic on an elemental atomic-percent basis: Nb, Zr, Ti, and Hf are each 20 at.%, while Mo and Ta are each 10 at.%.
